claims.text: Negative social well-being is positively associated with levels of interpersonal media use such as phone and online communication among young girls.
Negative social well-being is positively associated with non-interpersonal media use such as video, music, and reading among young girls.
Video use is strongly associated with negative social well-being indicators in young girls.
Media multitasking is associated with negative social indicators in young girls.
Face-to-face communication is strongly associated with positive social well-being in young girls.
Cell phone ownership has little direct association with children's socioemotional well-being.
Having a television or computer in one's room has little direct association with children's socioemotional well-being.
A granular measure of media multitasking was developed for assessing media use in young girls.
A comparative measure of media use versus time spent in face-to-face communication was introduced.

evidence.description: Regression analyses indicated that negative social well-being was positively associated with levels of uses of media that are centrally about interpersonal interaction (e.g., phone, online communication).
Regression analyses indicated that negative social well-being was positively associated with uses of media that are not centrally about interpersonal interaction (e.g., video, music, and reading).
Video use was particularly strongly associated with negative social well-being indicators.
Media multitasking was also associated with negative social indicators.
Conversely, face-to-face communication was strongly associated with positive social well-being.
Cell phone ownership and having a television or computer in one's room had little direct association with children's socioemotional well-being.

methodologies.name: Online survey and regression analysis
methodologies.description: An online survey measuring media use, media multitasking, face-to-face communication, and socioemotional well-being analyzed using regression models.
datasets: Discovery Girls magazine online survey dataset (N=3,461)

limitations.text: The study design does not address or establish causality between media use patterns and social well-being.

future_work.text: Develop research designs specifically capable of addressing causal relationships between media use, face-to-face interaction, and socioemotional well-being.
